auth_fix_acceptance.check3_class_sweep: PASS 24/24 - A-class 12 inline bootstraps all gone, B-class 5 admin consoles absorbed, C-class 7 each in place, no fourth helper (radar-session.ts extended), no duplicate paths, both route versions line-for-line equivalent. Constraint 3 confirmed: AuthButton's useState(!getCachedUser()) is now `status === 'loading'`, the sessionStorage dependency removed entirely.
auth_fix_acceptance.check2_s0_module: PASS at module level. Verified by READING THE ASSERTIONS, not the 22/22 count: old schema rebuilt to v1, warnings.length >= 1, malformed JSON survivable, storage-refusing device still gets a usable object. All three checklist pass-conditions covered.
auth_fix_acceptance.check2_structural_finding: Stronger than a browser observation: the failure chain is structurally eliminated, not merely guarded. authLoading now comes from useRadarSession() status and no longer from any page-local effect, and read() moved into its own draft-restoring effect. Even if read() still threw it could not stall authLoading. S0 and S4 are two independent defences.
auth_fix_acceptance.check1_login_button: NOT VERIFIED BY THE ACCEPTANCE OWNER. platform_eng self-tested and passed, but self-verification is what D48's separation exists to prevent. Recorded as 'implementer self-tested, acceptance owner has no capability'.
auth_fix_acceptance.browser_block_measured: Measured this shift by actually calling the tools: list_connected_browsers OK, tabs_context_mcp OK, tabs_close_mcp OK, select_browser DENIED (don't ask mode), navigate BLOCKED by the auto-mode classifier. A tab can be opened but no page can be loaded. Same wall platform_eng hit from the other side, so 'have the other side verify it' holds for nobody. Unrelated to the registry computer_use grant, which only opens three FB scripts.
auth_fix_acceptance.c8_my_own_miss: components/OpsConsole.tsx:363-380 is an inline getSession().then() with no .catch plus its own onAuthStateChange, and it was NOT in the 24-site table this department produced. platform_eng implemented all 24 they were given; they had no way to know. Responsibility is the spec author's. Low severity: loading starts false so render is not gated, but on rejection sessionToken stays null, hasCredential is false and :464 returns early, so data is never fetched - the same silent failure as C7, on /admin/ops. Filed as C8, does not block this round's definition of done.
auth_fix_acceptance.c8_root_cause: The original sweep claimed '31 grep hits, minus comments and the owner itself, 27 sites total' - a population was in hand but never reconciled line by line, and the shortfall was waved through with a summary phrase. Written into skills/evidence-not-absence/SKILL.md as case 3 plus a new rule: exhaustive means reconciled item by item, not a wide enough query.

computer_use_grant.but_does_not_unblock_acceptance: MEASURED, not inferred. scripts/org/org_attach.py:245-251 maps computer_use to exactly three Bash allowances - fb_realchrome_post.py, mark_fb_post_status.py, fb_page_post.py - all Facebook publishing. None of them can view our own site. The comment at :243-244 additionally forbids MCP and headless browsers.
computer_use_grant.mcp_browser_is_ungated: MEASURED. With no re-attach and zero capability rules in storage/org/runtime/member_success.settings.json (generated 22:34, before the 22:45 grant), list_connected_browsers still returned 8 connected Chromes. Browser access was never gated by the registry. Policy forbids MCP while the mechanism permits it - sent to governance 2026-08-05T14:51Z as a P2 request. Until governance rules, do NOT drive the browser via MCP for acceptance.
computer_use_grant.restore_not_run: org_attach.py restore is one-shot recovery after a reboot. There was no reboot; org_attach.py status showed all 8 panes live and this department holding the w1:p2J lease. Running it would disturb live panes and would only add the three FB scripts anyway.

anonymous_context_trap: Probing destroys what it probes. Of the 8 connected Chromes only 398dcdba-2b52-427b-8877-aab67cda72cd is identified - the owner's main Chrome with a live VolPred admin session, the exact opposite of what acceptance check 1 needs. Finding a clean one by trial requires navigating each candidate to our site, which turns it into a browser that has visited the site - and check 1 explicitly forbids using one. So no candidate was probed. A clean context can only come from an incognito window or a fresh profile, i.e. one owner action. When it is obtained, write the deviceId and identity back into the user memory reference_chrome_browser_identity_map so no future shift has to ask again.
expiring_measurement: What an ANONYMOUS visitor saw BEFORE the fix can only be measured before platform_eng deploys S1/S3/S4, which is their next shift. After that it is unmeasurable forever (the checklist already states a post-fix observation cannot be back-projected). Recommendation sent to manager: capture it only if the owner is already at the machine; otherwise let D25 row 5 state post-fix observation only and record that pre-fix anonymous behaviour is no longer measurable. An honest hole beats an inferred number.

Two rulings are outstanding: manager (P1 sent 14:50Z, three items - which authorisation route the acceptance browser takes, who produces the clean anonymous context on deploy day, and whether tonight's expiring baseline is worth one owner interruption) and governance (P2 sent 14:51Z, policy-vs-mechanism conflict). Not driving the browser via MCP until governance rules.

shift_environment_note: 2026-08-05 shift 8: bare `git`, `python3 -c`, and `ls` of paths outside the repo were denied by the permission layer; `ls`/`cat`/`grep`/`uv run` and every scripts/org/ CLI worked. Consequence: a shift may be unable to inspect git state directly - use scripts/ops_snapshot.py for git, and let scripts/git_writer_lock.py commit be the thing that proves what is or is not tracked. Do not assume a file is committed because it exists on disk.
